facts: A **vertex** (plural **vertices**) is a dot in the network. An **edge** joins two vertices or loops back to the same vertex.
The **degree** of a vertex is the number of edge-ends meeting at it.
A **loop** joins a vertex to itself and adds $2$ to that vertex's degree.
**Multiple edges** between the same pair of vertices are allowed, and each one is counted separately.
Every edge has two ends, so the **sum of all the degrees is $2\times$ the number of edges** and is always even.
Two edges that cross on the page do **not** meet at a vertex unless a dot is drawn there.
Moving the vertices or bending the edges gives a **different drawing of the same network**, provided the same named vertices are joined and any arrows and weights stay the same.

foundation.question_text:
A network represents a school's messaging app. Two students are connected by an edge when they are messaging partners.
What do the vertices and edges represent?
foundation.solution_text:
Each object in this network is a student, so the vertices represent students.
Each connection is a messaging partnership, so the edges represent messaging partnerships between students.
